title: Varun Dhawan Is in Talks for a Hollywood Action Film With the Producer of Mortal Kombat. Here’s What That Actually Means.
excerpt: The Bollywood actor is reportedly in advanced negotiations with Lawrence Kasanoff for an inter-parallel-universe film. It’s not a done deal — but the conversation itself is the story.
body:
Varun Dhawan wants to go to Hollywood. This isn’t new — he once told an interviewer his dream was to be launched by Steven Spielberg, which is the kind of thing a 2014-era Bollywood star says when they’re feeling ambitious. But what’s happening now is different. It’s specific, it’s in negotiation, and it involves a producer whose name you’d recognise even if you’ve never watched a Bollywood film.

Lawrence Kasanoff — the man behind the *Mortal Kombat* franchise — is reportedly in advanced talks with Dhawan for an action film set in what’s being described as an “inter-parallel universe.” Multiple Indian entertainment outlets, including Zoom TV, Filmibeat, and MensXP, have confirmed that discussions are ongoing, though no deal has been officially announced.

## What We Know

The project is in early development. The concept involves parallel universes — a genre that Hollywood has been mining aggressively since *Everything Everywhere All at Once* won Best Picture. Kasanoff’s involvement suggests a film that leans more action-spectacle than art-house multiverse, which tracks with his filmography.

Kasanoff is best known for producing the original *Mortal Kombat* (1995) and its sequel, as well as building the gaming franchise into a film property. His recent work has focused on licensing, technology, and cross-media ventures. He’s not a Marvel-tier producer, but he’s a Hollywood figure with a specific niche: turning genre IPs into commercial films.

Dhawan’s team has reportedly been in “final negotiations,” though in Bollywood-to-Hollywood parlance, that can mean anything from “we’re signing next week” to “we had a good Zoom call.” No announcement is imminent.

## Why This Is Worth Watching

The obvious comparison is to other Bollywood actors who’ve moved to Hollywood: Priyanka Chopra via *Quantico* and the talent-management pipeline, Deepika Padukone via *xXx: Return of Xander Cage*, Ali Fazal via *Death on the Nile*, and Dhanush via *The Gray Man*. Each followed a slightly different route, but all involved Indian actors fitting into existing Hollywood productions as supporting or ensemble players.

What’s different about the Dhawan-Kasanoff conversation is the genre. An “inter-parallel universe action film” produced by the Mortal Kombat creator suggests a lead role in a genre-specific property — not a cultural-ambassador casting but a straightforward action star role. That’s rarer, and potentially more significant.

It’s also worth noting what Dhawan brings to the table commercially. He’s not India’s most critically acclaimed actor, but he has a genuine mass-audience following. His films have collectively grossed thousands of crores. He’s physically built for action roles. And at 39, he’s at the right age for the kind of physically demanding franchise role that a Kasanoff project would likely require.

## The NRI Angle

For the Indian diaspora — particularly younger NRIs who consume both Bollywood and Hollywood without much distinction — a Dhawan-led Hollywood film would sit in an interesting space. He’s not the crossover choice that film critics would pick (that would be someone like Rajkummar Rao or Vikrant Massey). He’s the mainstream choice — the actor your cousin in Dallas watches on JioHotstar every Friday night.

That mainstream appeal is actually what makes this commercially interesting for Kasanoff. A parallel-universe action film with a Bollywood star gives you automatic access to the Indian and NRI market without requiring the Indian audience to “discover” an unfamiliar actor. Dhawan already has the audience. Kasanoff just needs to point them at a new kind of film.

## What Could Go Wrong

Plenty. Hollywood-Bollywood crossovers have a painful track record. Priyanka Chopra’s Hollywood career has been more strategic than spectacular. Deepika’s *xXx* sequel underperformed. Irrfan Khan’s Hollywood work was brilliant but never broke through commercially in the way his Indian films did.

The gap between “in talks” and “in production” is where most of these deals quietly die. Dhawan’s upcoming Bollywood release, *Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai*, arrives on June 5 — and if that film underperforms, the negotiating leverage shifts.

## The Bottom Line

This isn’t a done deal. It may never become one. But the conversation itself tells you something about where Indian cinema’s commercial ambitions are heading: not just into foreign festivals or streaming platforms, but into the genre-franchise space that Hollywood dominates. If Varun Dhawan ends up in a parallel-universe action film produced by the Mortal Kombat creator, it won’t be the prestige crossover. It’ll be the commercial one. And that might matter more.
nri_angle: For NRIs who navigate between Bollywood and Hollywood daily, a Dhawan-Kasanoff deal represents the kind of crossover that is still exceedingly rare.
